_comment: Bonds with Ash for the core cast (issue #50, DESIGN.md 5.10). ranks: bond points needed for rank 1..5 (index 0 = rank 0). Points come from the first chat each day in Hollowmark (talk), each day spent in a role they like (liked_role) or dislike (disliked_role), expeditions that come home with a success (expedition), fighting beside Ash (mission, per kill_step kills) and the choices in rank scenes. Points never drop below the current rank, and stop at the next rank until its scene is seen. Rank 5 also needs their personal mission (data/personal.json, a short playable mission on the Command Table, issue #113) done; it unlocks at rank 4. likes / dislikes: role or role:target as Empire.recruits stores them. perks: rank -> {name, desc, effect}; effects are read in empire.gd (bond_perks_with / bond_perk_total). Effect keys: gilt, supplies, insight (a day), gilt_per_held (a day per province held), heal, research_pace, squad_odds, all_odds, surge_warning, job_speed (expeditions take this much less time), build_discount (off building and Wardlamp Gilt), standing_bonus (added to every faction standing gain), fray_home (less Hollowmark Fray a day), mission_hp, mission_damage, mission_revive, mission_guard (less damage taken), mission_power_rate (faster gauge). Scene lines: [speaker id, text] or [speaker id, text, expression] (assets/portraits/<id>_<expression>.png, falling back to <id>.png); speaker "" is narration. Ash never speaks: choices are what Ash does. Romance (a moment scene between rank 3 and 4, a romantic rank 5 variant), friends and rivals, and epilogues live in data/relationships.json and data/epilogues.json (issue #116).

bran.likes_text: being sent somewhere to hit things (party, expeditions)

3.name: Rider Clause
3.desc: +10 max HP for the party on missions.

5.name: Paid in Full
5.desc: +3 damage for the party on missions.

scenes.title: Terms and Conditions
lines: bran
Since we're stuck together, let's go over the terms. I 'it things. You point. Nobody gets sentimental.
He rolls up his sleeve. The contract is tattooed from wrist to elbow, in a cramped clerk's hand.
bran
Clause four: I guard the client. Clause nine: someone pays more, I tell the client first. Then I'm off.
bran
It tightens if I break it. Like a fist. Ask me 'ow I know.

choice.label: [Read the small print]
reply: Ha. Nobody reads the small print. Clause twelve says I get the good chair. Sit somewhere else.

choice.label: [Shake his hand]
reply: Firm. Silent. You'd make a terrible merchant and a great witness.

choice.label: [Shrug]
reply: Fair. I wouldn't trust me neither. That's why it's wrote down.

scenes.title: Who Holds the Pen
lines: bran
You keep looking at the arm. Go on, then.
bran
Gallows Ferry. Eighteen. Signed with the Ferrymen's Guild 'cause they fed you before the work, not after.
bran
Their notary inked it on me so I couldn't lose it. Or sell it. Or forget whose I was.
He flexes. The letters ripple and settle, like they're listening.
bran
Guild sold me contract on four times. Never met the man 'oo holds it now.

choice.label: [Touch the ink]
reply: Warm, isn't it? It's always warm. Like it's alive and annoyed about it.

choice.label: [Point at yourself: no contract]
reply: No Ledger, no contract, no name. Must be nice. Or terrifyin'. Can't tell from 'ere.

scenes.title: A Better Offer
lines: bran
Clause nine. Said you'd 'ear it first, so 'ere it is.
bran
Concord man found me at the gate. Two 'undred Gilt for a letter saying where you sleep.
bran
That's more'n you pay me in a season. I did the sums twice.
He doesn't move. Neither does the tattoo.
bran
Thing is, the arm never tightened. Not a twinge. So either the contract's broke, or I am.

choice.label: [Offer him a raise]
reply: Put that away. I said I'd tell you. Never said I'd take it. Keep your coin. For now.

choice.label: [Wait]
reply: Right. You trust me to make the call. That's either very smart or very stupid. Sent 'im 'ome with a bruise.

choice.label: [Hand him the letter paper]
reply: Testin' me? Fine. Bad joke, though. I'll remember it at invoice time.

end: bran
From now on I fight like I mean it. Don't make it weird.

scenes.title: The Holder
lines: bran
Found 'im. The man who holds me paper. Broker on Gallows Ferry, buys contracts by the barrel.
bran
I want to buy meself back. Or rewrite it. Or put his head through the counting-house window. Ain't decided.
bran
I ain't asking for a favour. I'm asking for a squad and a couple of days. Billed to me.
He picks at the edge of the ink. For once he doesn't look at you while he talks.

choice.label: [Nod: go]
reply: Good. Gallows Ferry, on the Command Table. It's marked personal, which I 'ate. You're coming.

choice.label: [Point at the map: take friends]
reply: Friends. Sure. Witnesses, more like. Brokers behave better with witnesses.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Buy Back the Paper", at Gallows Ferry. Bran is going, and Ash goes with him.

scenes.title: Blank Clause
lines: bran
Look.
The tattoo is still there, every clause. But where the holder's name was, the skin is clean.
bran
I paid 'im. Then I made him strike his own name out. Then I may have thrown the pen in the river.
bran
So the contract's with nobody now. Means I'm 'ere 'cause I want to be. Disgustin'.
bran
Don't tell no one. I got a reputation.

choice.label: [Smile]
reply: Stop that. I'm still sending you an invoice. For the pen.

choice.label: [Write "Ash" in the blank space with a finger]
reply: ...Huh. Didn't take. You ain't got a name to write. That's fine. I know 'oo it's for.

gristle.likes_text: the Infirmary, and fieldwork with plenty of wounds
gristle.dislikes_text: the Coven, and sitting around unbilled

3.name: House Calls
3.desc: Injured people heal 1 extra day each day.

scenes.title: Your Account
lines: gristle
Sit. No, there. That's the chair for people who pay later, that is.
She opens a ledger thicker than her arm. Your page already has entries.
gristle
Splinter, three copper. Watching me work, one copper. Breathing in my shop, I'm being generous.
gristle
Don't look like that. Everyone owes Mother Gristle. It's how you know you're alive, isn't it.

choice.label: [Pay a coin]
reply: Oh, a payer. Rare, that is. Suspicious, too. I'll keep an eye on you, dearie.

choice.label: [Pull out an empty pocket]
reply: Ha! Honest poverty. My favourite customer, you are. Interest is charged weekly.

choice.label: [Point at Bran's entry]
reply: Disputes every line, he does. I add a line for the disputing. Very happy, we are.

scenes.title: Same Bottles
lines: gristle
Hold this. Don't drink it.
She hands you a green bottle. Then an identical green bottle.
gristle
One's for fever. One's for husbands. Same bottle, isn't it. Different spoon.
gristle
Medicine and poison, opposites? Same thing in different amounts, they are. And amounts are a matter of price.

choice.label: [Hand both back carefully]
reply: Careful hands, those are. You'd make a decent apprentice if you could scream for help.

choice.label: [Sniff one]
reply: Brave, that was. The husband one, you've had. You'll be fine. Probably. Sit down an hour.

scenes.title: The Assessor
lines: gristle
You want to know why the Coven threw me out. Everyone does, in the end. On the bill, it is.
gristle
A Concord assessor came to the woods to write down what we were worth. Took sick, he did. I treated him.
gristle
Generously. Repeatedly. Until there was nothing left of him to assess.
gristle
The Coven said I'd brought the Concord down on us. Right, they were. The Concord brought the Blank.
She wipes the same clean bottle for a long time.

choice.label: [Sit with her]
reply: Hm. Quiet company. You don't even charge for it. You should, you know.

choice.label: [Nod: he had it coming]
reply: Oh, he did. Doesn't mean I sleep, does it. Means I sleep less badly.

end: gristle
Send me your wounded. I'll keep them alive. Mostly to bill them.

scenes.title: One Debt Owed
lines: gristle
Everyone owes me. One person owes me a life.
gristle
Hester Vane, Coven elder. Pulled her grandson out of a fever, I did, when nobody else would touch him.
gristle
Voted me out the next spring, she did. I've let that debt grow interest for eleven years.
gristle
Time to collect, it is. Not coin. I want my name back on the tree. Lend me a squad.

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Good. Gutterwoods, when you're ready. Bring the strong ones. A temper, Hester has, and a lot of nephews.

choice.label: [Mime: gently]
reply: Gently. Yes. I'll ask very gently. With a very large bottle in the other hand.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Collect from Hester Vane", in the Gutterwoods. Mother Gristle is going, and Ash goes with her.

scenes.title: Paid in Full
lines: gristle
My name's back on the tree. Carved deep, so the white has to work for it.
gristle
Hester cried. Billed her for the tissue, I did. We're even now. Horrible, it is. Never been even with anyone.
She opens the ledger to your page and draws a line through every entry.
gristle
Don't get used to it. A one-time professional courtesy, this is.

choice.label: [Pay her anyway]
reply: ...You absolute fool. Fine. Fine! New page. Look what you've done.

choice.label: [Bow]
reply: Get up, you'll ruin your back and then you'll owe me again, won't you.

ninefingers.likes_text: fighting, and drilling the recruits at the Barracks

3.name: Covering Fire
3.desc: +10% success on expeditions Daro goes on.

5.name: Reads the Orders
5.desc: +1 day of warning before every Blank surge.

scenes.title: The Finger
lines: ninefingers
Staring at the hand. Everybody stares at the hand.
ninefingers
Fine. Lost it to a paper cut. Form C-114, Requisition of Requisition Forms. Went septic.
Bran, passing: "Last week it was a bear."
ninefingers
Last week I liked you more, Tolley.

choice.label: [Hold up nine fingers]
reply: Oh, that's funny. Silent and a comedian. Going to get along bloody horribly.

choice.label: [Look concerned]
reply: Don't. Pity's a form too. I don't sign those.

scenes.title: Old Habits
lines: ninefingers
Saluted the scarecrow again this morning. Then filed a report on it in my head.
ninefingers
Twelve years in. Don't train you to fight. Train you to stand still while some sir reads at you.
ninefingers
Still wake at fourth bell for roll call. Count myself. Nine, ten. Nine. Always nine.

choice.label: [Salute them]
reply: ...Dismissed, smart-mouth. Actually, that was all right. Don't do it again.

choice.label: [Offer a drink]
reply: Tobble's? He'll want a secret for the second. Got plenty. None he can afford.

scenes.title: The Order
lines: ninefingers
Want to know why I walked. Fine. Once. Then we never talk about it.
ninefingers
Hob's Wick. Forty people, a chapel, a mill. The Concord ruled it had "no material use". Erasure order, signed and sealed.
ninefingers
Orders were to strike it from the Ledger. Blank does the rest. Clean, bloodless, paperwork. Nobody gets their kit dirty.
ninefingers
Tore the order in half. Lieutenant took the finger as a fine. Then I walked.
They say it like a weather report. Their hands are shaking.

choice.label: [Put a hand on their shoulder]
reply: Yeah. Yeah, all right. Two seconds. Then it's weird.

choice.label: [Nod slowly]
reply: That's it. Right reaction. Everyone else asks if it was worth a finger.

end: ninefingers
Send me out with the squads. I watch backs. Only thing they taught me that's any good.

scenes.title: Hob's Wick
lines: ninefingers
Never went back. Never checked. If the order got signed again by some sir with all his fingers...
ninefingers
Off Tithe Road. Two days through Concord toll posts with my face on a poster.
ninefingers
Need to know. Even if it's white. Especially if it's white.

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Right. Tithe Road. Going in a hood. A big one. Bring someone who talks to guards.

choice.label: [Point at their poster, then shrug]
reply: Likeness is terrible, anyway. Gave me ten fingers. Amateurs.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Find Hob's Wick", on the Tithe Road. Daro is going, and Ash goes with them.

scenes.title: Roll of Honour
lines: ninefingers
It's there. Whole village. Mill's turning. Kids. Goats. Bad beer.
ninefingers
And in the chapel, a plaque. "Corporal Daro, fallen against the Blank." Concord declared me dead so they wouldn't have to say deserted.
ninefingers
Forty civvies pray for me every week. Think I'm a hero who died. Didn't have the heart to correct them.
ninefingers
First time dead. Roomier than expected.

choice.label: [Count their fingers with them: nine]
reply: Nine. Yeah. Nine's fine. Nine's what it cost. Cheap, really.

choice.label: [Salute]
reply: Stop that. ...Fine. Back at you, Unwritten.

quill.likes_text: the Command Table, running Hollowmark, or haggling with the Guild

scenes.title: Two Sets of Books
lines: quill
A quartermaster keeps two sets of books, per regulations. One for the Concord, which is beautiful. One for us, which is true.
quill
Which would you like to see? Most commanders want the beautiful one. It has margins.
Two ledgers sit on the stores counter: one bound in red leather, one in sacking.

choice.label: [Point at the true one]
reply: Oh, good. A grown-up. It's grim reading. We have eleven days of turnips and an outstanding debt in respect of a goat.

choice.label: [Point at the beautiful one]
reply: Lovely, isn't it? Every number a lie, every lie in a perfect hand. You'll want the other one eventually.

scenes.title: Written Off
lines: quill
Do you know what "written off" means in Concord books? A debt duly deemed uncollectable. A cost with no return.
quill
A village can be written off. A road. A person. Once they're off the books, the Ledger stops seeing them.
quill
And what the Ledger doesn't see, the Blank eats. Very tidy. Very efficient. I was very good at it.
Quill closes the ledger gently, the way you'd close a coffin.

choice.label: [Tap the true ledger: keep writing]
reply: Yes. That's the job now, isn't it? Writing people back in. Badly. In pencil. Still counts, as it were.

choice.label: [Frown]
reply: Yes, well. I frown at myself too. Twice daily, with meals.

scenes.title: The List
lines: quill
I kept a list. Every line I wrote off, every name. Thirty-one.
A folded page, soft from handling. Names in a neat, careful hand.
quill
I check them against the Blank reports. Nine are gone. The rest are still holding, somewhere.
quill
I'm moving money to them. Quietly. A coin here, a sack of seed there, under "sundries". I took it from your budget. I'm telling you because you'd find out.

choice.label: [Nod: keep doing it]
reply: ...Thank you. I'll make it back. I'll make it back twice. Watch the ledger.

choice.label: [Hold out a hand for the list]
reply: No. Sorry. That one's mine to carry. But I'll read you the names some night, if you like.

end: quill
From now on the beautiful books pay for the true ones. Expect a little more Gilt each day. Don't ask how.

scenes.title: The Original
lines: quill
The list is a copy. The original ledger, the one with my signature on every line, is held at Old Mill Crossing in a Concord strongbox, pending review.
quill
As long as it exists, those thirty-one stay written off. It's the official record.
quill
If it went missing, or caught fire, or was very carefully corrected in my hand...
quill
I'd need to go myself. Nobody else can forge me. I've checked.

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Old Mill Crossing, then. Bring someone with a crowbar. I'll bring the good pen. I don't fight, so you will.

choice.label: [Mime striking a match]
reply: Tempting. But burning leaves a gap, and the Blank loves a gap. No. I'm going to fix it.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Correct the Original", at Old Mill Crossing. Quill can't fight: the party goes along to keep them alive.

scenes.title: Balanced
lines: quill
Done. Thirty-one lines corrected. "Written off" became "carried forward". The Ledger sees them again.
quill
I also added one entry, herewith. I hope you don't mind.
At the bottom of the page, in Quill's best hand: "ASH. Owes nothing. Is owed nothing. Balanced."
quill
It won't stick, of course. You're not in the Ledger. But it's in mine.

choice.label: [Run a finger over the line]
reply: It's the only honest entry in the book. Don't tell the Concord. They'd audit it.

choice.label: [Bow]
reply: Oh, stop. Get back to work. We have eleven days of turnips.

tobble.likes_text: minding the tavern (idle) and talking to anyone (envoy)

3.name: Loose Lips
3.desc: +1 Insight a day from tavern gossip.

scenes.title: The Second Drink
lines: tobble
First drink's free. House rule. Second costs thee a secret.
He slides a mug across. It is mostly foam and history.
tobble
Most folk pay with gossip. Who's sleeping where, who owes who. You, though. You don't talk.
tobble
So what's a silent customer pay with, eh?

choice.label: [Draw a little picture in the foam]
reply: Ha! A goat? A cloud? A goat in a cloud. Worth a drink. Worth two. Don't tell the others.

choice.label: [Leave the second drink]
reply: Sensible. Most sensible customer I've had in thirty years. Bit dull.

choice.label: [Put a coin down]
reply: Coin's fine. Coin's honest. Secrets are better, but you'll warm up, lad. Or lass. Whichever.

scenes.title: Retiring Next Week
lines: tobble
Retiring next week. Got a cottage picked out. Frayed Meadow, by the brook. Roses.
tobble
Course, half the Meadow's gone white. Might be the brook half. Might be the rose half.
tobble
Been retiring next week for thirty year. Keeps me young. Thinking about it, anyway.

choice.label: [Mime: one more week]
reply: One more week. Aye. That's the spirit. Always one more.

choice.label: [Point at his knees]
reply: Don't you start. Me knees and I have an arrangement. They grumble and I ignore 'em.

scenes.title: The Secret I Sold
lines: tobble
I'll tell thee one I never sell. Sold it once, and that were enough.
tobble
Years back, a lass hid in my cellar. Abbey runaway, like our Sister. A man paid well to know where.
tobble
I told him. Next morning the cellar were clean. Not empty. Clean. White as new paper.
tobble
That's the Blank. It doesn't just eat. It's hired.
He polishes a mug that was clean when he started.

choice.label: [Sit at the bar a while]
reply: Aye. Stay. It's the only payment for that one. Somebody staying.

choice.label: [Nod: you know now]
reply: There. I'm lighter by one. Funny, I reckoned I'd feel worse.

end: tobble
My regulars talk. I'll pass along owt worth reading. On the house. Mostly.

scenes.title: The Old Sign
lines: tobble
Before Hollowmark I had a place in the Meadow. The Last Drop. Best ale on the Tithe Road, and nowt else close.
tobble
Roof's gone now. The Blank's at the doorstep. But the sign's still hanging. Saw it from the ridge.
tobble
I want it. Daft, I know. A board with a mug painted on it. But it's mine.
tobble
Knees and all, I'm going. Send someone to carry us back.

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Good lad. Good... whatever tha art. The Meadow, by the white. I'll bring the ladder. You bring the swinging.

choice.label: [Offer to carry him]
reply: Cheek! I'll walk. I'll complain the whole way, but I'll walk.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Fetch the Last Drop's Sign", in the Frayed Meadow. Old Tobble can't fight: the party goes along to keep him alive.

scenes.title: Last Orders
lines: The old sign hangs over the tavern door now: a mug, a crack, and THE LAST DROP in flaking gold.
tobble
Looks right, doesn't it? Like it were always meant to be here.
tobble
I've decided summat. I'm not retiring next week.
tobble
Somebody has to pour at the end of the world. Might as well be him as knows where the good barrel is.

choice.label: [Raise a mug]
reply: To the last drop. And the one after it, if we're lucky.

choice.label: [Point at the sign, then at him]
reply: Aye. Both of us cracked and still hanging on. Go on, drink's free. Both of 'em.

abeyance.dislikes_text: being in charge of people, or talking to them officially

scenes.title: Your Name
lines: abeyance
The page rewrote itself again last night. Deo gratias, I copy it out every morning so I don't lose what it said.
She shows you her notebook. Each entry is different. The last one is a single word, written over and over.
abeyance
It wrote your name. Which is odd, because you don't have one.
abeyance
I can't read it. I mean the letters won't stay still. But it's yours. I'd know it anywhere.

choice.label: [Lean in to look]
reply: Do you see it? No? It goes shy when you look at it. Like you do.

choice.label: [Step back]
reply: Sorry. That's a lot, isn't it. The Abbey said I was too much as well. Sister Werburgh said it daily.

scenes.title: The Polite Voices
lines: abeyance
People ask about the voices. They expect me to be frightened.
abeyance
They're very polite. They say please. They say excuse me. They ask what year it is. God keep them.
abeyance
I think they're the erased. Everyone the Blank took. They don't know they're gone, so they keep asking for directions.
abeyance
I give them directions. To where, I don't know. Somewhere with a door.

choice.label: [Sit and listen with her]
reply: ...One of them just said hello to you. You're the first person they've noticed. Interesting.

choice.label: [Offer her tea]
reply: Thank you. They like tea too. Well. The idea of tea.

scenes.title: What the Abbey Teaches
lines: abeyance
At the Abbey they teach that the Ledger is truth. Quod scriptum est. If it is written, it is. If it is struck out, it never was.
abeyance
I copied Erasure orders for six years. Beautiful work. My serifs were famous, God forgive me.
abeyance
Then the page came to me, and every night it wrote back something I'd struck out. A name. A street. A dog.
abeyance
Truth isn't what's written. Truth is what refuses to stay crossed out.

choice.label: [Point at yourself]
reply: Yes. Exactly. You're the best argument I've ever met. I may write a treatise on you.

choice.label: [Hand her a fresh quill]
reply: Oh, a good one. I'll use it for the margins. That's where I keep the true things now.

end: abeyance
I'll work the margins at the Scriptorium. Things go faster when you know what to look for.

scenes.title: A Map
lines: abeyance
The page drew a map last night. Not words. Lines. The Wickham Hills, and a chapel I've never seen.
abeyance
There's an X. The page has never been that direct. It's usually so polite.
abeyance
I think it wants to go home. Or it wants me to see something. I must take it. Will you send people with me?

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Thank you. The Wickham Hills. I'll pack the notebook. And the page. Obviously the page. You'll have to do the fighting.

choice.label: [Mime: careful]
reply: I'm always careful. It's the page that isn't.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Follow the Page", in the Wickham Hills. Sister Hild can't fight: the party goes along to keep her alive.

scenes.title: Not Yet
lines: abeyance
The chapel was empty. Just a lectern, and on it, a book with every page torn out but one.
abeyance
My page fit the gap exactly. It went in, and the book wrote one line, and then it was still. Fiat.
abeyance
I copied it for you. It's about you, I think. I'm almost sure.
She hands you a slip of paper. In her famous serifs: NOT YET.
abeyance
I don't know if it's a warning or a promise. I think it a promise. The Abbot would call that pride.

choice.label: [Fold it into your coat]
reply: Keep it close. And if it ever changes, tell me. Well. Show me.

choice.label: [Take her hand]
reply: Oh. The voices have gone quiet. All of them. That's never happened. Stay a moment. Please.

ottoline.likes_text: fighting up front (party), or keeping Hollowmark's door (governing Hollowmark)
ottoline.dislikes_text: being polite to officials, and books

3.name: House Rules
3.desc: The party takes 10% less damage on missions.

5.name: Nobody Gets Through
5.desc: Hollowmark's Fray falls by 1 more each day.

scenes.title: The List
lines: ottoline
Stop. Name?
She looks down at Ash from a long way up. She has a slate in one hand and a stub of chalk in the other.
ottoline
Right. You haven't got one. That's a first. Everyone's got a name, even a fake. Specially a fake.
ottoline
Thirty year our Tobble's kept a list of who drinks here. I keep the list of who doesn't. It's shorter. More teeth in it.
ottoline
So. Which list are you on?
smug

choice.label: [Point at the first list]
reply: Bold. Fine. You're on it. In chalk. Chalk rubs off, so behave.

choice.label: [Take the chalk and draw a little door]
reply: She studies the door for a long time.
...That's not a name. That's better than a name. Nobody gets through a door without me. You're in.

choice.label: [Try to walk past her]
reply: She doesn't move. She doesn't have to. Ash bounces off.
Second list. Try again tomorrow. Bring manners.

scenes.title: Six Hundred Sequins
lines: Ottoline is sewing. Her hands are the size of shovels and the needle is the size of an eyelash. She does not miss a stitch.
ottoline
Sequins. Fauvette's old costume needed six hundred. Every one came off once a week at least, usually in a fight.
ottoline
Rule of the Crimson Encore: if the audience can see you, you're part of the show. So the bouncers wore sequins too.
ottoline
I were the biggest sparkle in the room. Glittering at drunks. Throwing them out in time with the band.
ottoline
Don't laugh. Had a waltz for it. Three steps, a turn, out the door.
happy

choice.label: [Bow and offer a hand: show me]
reply: She takes the hand. Three steps. A turn. Somehow Ash is outside, the door is shut, and nothing hurts.
That's the waltz. Gentle as you like. That's how the magistrate felt. Well. He got the rough version.

choice.label: [Hold the thread for her]
reply: Steady hands. Good. Most folk shake round me. I'm told it's the height.

scenes.title: Six Tickets
lines: ottoline
Fauvette'll tell you about the night the Blank came down Lantern Row, if she hasn't. Her version's got a lot of swooning in it.
ottoline
Here's mine. The white came up the street like milk boiling over. Everyone ran for the door. My door.
ottoline
Got them out. Two at a time, three. Threw people. And I counted. Hundred and twelve in. Hundred and six out.
ottoline
Then it were on the step, and I could hear the last six coming down off the balcony, laughing, they didn't know yet. And I shut the door.
sad
ottoline
If I hadn't, it'd have followed them out into the street. Into all of us. That's the sum. Done it every night since.
She opens her fist. Six coat-check tickets, tied with a bit of red ribbon.

choice.label: [Stand beside her, the way she stands by a door]
reply: ...Yeah. Like that. Nobody's ever kept the door for me. Boring, isn't it? Give over.

choice.label: [Touch the tickets]
reply: Careful. They're still warm. Six year and they're still warm. Pell says that means summat. Told Pell to shut up.

choice.label: [Nod: you saved a hundred and six]
reply: Everyone says that. Like it's a sum that comes out even. It doesn't. You can't subtract people.

end: ottoline
Right. Nobody lays a finger on the party while I'm there. House rules. I'll be stood in front of you, so try not to get in my way.

scenes.title: Knocking
lines: ottoline
Pell came to see us. Says there's a sound at Lantern Row, on Gallows Ferry. Where the Encore stood, before the white took the street.
ottoline
Knocking. From inside the white. Six knocks, then a wait, then six knocks.
ottoline
Could be nowt. Could be the Blank doing an impression. It does that. Learns your voice. Learns the people you lost.
ottoline
I've kept that door shut six year. I want to be the one who opens it. Or the one who checks it's still shut. Either road, I'm going.
angry

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Good. Lantern Row, on Gallows Ferry. Bring people who don't scare easy, and someone to hold my coat.

choice.label: [Point at yourself: I'm coming]
reply: No. You run the town. Send me with a squad and I'll send you a postcard. ...Fine. You can wave me off. Wave like you mean it.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Answer the Knocking", at Gallows Ferry. Big Ottoline is going, and Ash goes with her.

scenes.title: Coat Check
lines: Ottoline comes in out of the weather, soaked to the skin, carrying six coats over her arm like sleeping children.
ottoline
It were the door. Just the door, stood in the white, nowt round it. My chalk marks still on the frame.
ottoline
I knocked back. Six times. Then I opened it.
ottoline
Nowt behind it but the cloakroom. Six coats on six hooks. No people. Just the coats, waiting to be collected.
sad
ottoline
So I collected them. You hand the ticket over, you get your coat, you go home. Hung them on the old tree in the plaza.
ottoline
Summat knocked once more as I left. Just once. Could've been a draught. I've decided it were a thank you.
happy

choice.label: [Hand her a fresh stick of chalk]
reply: For the list? Go on, then. No. You go on it in proper ink. Chalk's for strangers.

choice.label: [Hold the door open for her]
reply: Ha! Look at you. Manners. I'll make a bouncer of you yet. Now shift, you're letting the draught in.

jessamy.likes_text: running jobs on the roads (expeditions), and dealing with the Guild
jessamy.dislikes_text: desk work by daylight (governing, the Command Table)

scenes.title: Contraband
lines: It is very late. Jessamy is sitting on the tavern roof with her boots dangling, eating somebody else's apple.
jessamy
Oh, hello, handsome. Or pretty. It's dark, I'm generous, and you're a bit of a blur, cully. Come up.
jessamy
Do you know what you are, to a girl in my trade? The finest contraband in the Inklands.
jessamy
No papers, no name, no line in the Ledger. Nobody can tax you, the pennies can't stop you at a toll. You're a crate with nothin' written on it.
smug
jessamy
I could move you anywhere. Very discreet. For a price, which we'd discuss over somethin' stronger than this apple.

choice.label: [Climb up and sit beside her]
reply: There. Now we're both breaking a by-law. Rooftop loitering, two counts. Don't tell the Concord, they'll fine us in fractions.

choice.label: [Hold out a hand for the apple]
reply: Cheeky. It's stolen, you know. That's why it tastes like that. Here, half. Now you're on the cross with me.

choice.label: [Stay on the ground]
reply: Suit yourself. The view's better from up here. Of you, mostly.

scenes.title: Don't Ask
lines: jessamy
Six years I've run crates down the Tithe Road. Never once opened one. Not even the ones that knocked.
jessamy
Some of them ticked. Some were warm. One hummed hymns all the way to Gallows Ferry, very quietly, in a man's voice.
jessamy
Not askin' is good manners, cully. Everyone's allowed one box nobody looks in.
She says it lightly. Then she checks the sky over the rooftops, the way sailors check for weather. Still dark. She relaxes.
jessamy
Go on, then. What's in your box?
smug

choice.label: [Open your empty hands]
reply: Nothin'? That's the saddest thing I've ever seen. Or the most suspicious. I'll decide which once I know you better.

choice.label: [Point back at her: you first]
reply: Ha. No. Nice try. Mine's nailed shut. ...I'll tell you one day. Not today. Today I'm bein' charmin'.

scenes.title: Struck Off
lines: Dawn is close. Jessamy keeps glancing at the eastern rooftops, the way you'd watch a dog you don't trust.
jessamy
All right. The box. Since you keep not askin', which is very unfair of you.
jessamy
I owed money to the wrong people. So I paid a scribe on the Tithe Road to strike me out of the Ledger. No entry, no debt. Clever girl.
jessamy
Turns out the Ledger isn't just who owes what. It's what holds you in the world. Take your line out and you start to thin.
sad
The first grey light touches her hand. Ash can see the roof tiles through her fingers.
jessamy
Sunlight goes straight through me. A little more every year. I'm a smuggler because I'm only allowed to exist after dark.
jessamy
That's why I like you, you know. You're the only other one. Except you're not fadin'. How do you do that?

choice.label: [Stand between her and the sunrise]
reply: ...Oh. Don't. You'll make me sentimental, and then I'll have to nick somethin' to feel like myself again.

choice.label: [Take her hand in the light]
reply: Can you feel it? I can't, not really. Just the idea of a hand. Hold on anyway. It's nice bein' held by someone nobody can write down either.

choice.label: [Shrug: you don't know]
reply: No. Course you don't. Neither of us read the instructions.

end: jessamy
I know every back road and every bent quartermaster between here and the sea. You'll have more Supplies than you know what to do with. Don't ask where from.
smug

scenes.title: The Notary
lines: jessamy
The scribe who struck me out. Notary Fennick. Still workin' a toll post on the Tithe Road, scratchin' people off for coin.
jessamy
A pen that can take you out can put you back in. If he's paid enough. Or frightened enough.
jessamy
Never wanted to be on anybody's books in my life. But I'd like to see noon again. Just once. I've forgotten what colour things are.
sad
jessamy
Lend me a squad. A big one. Fennick scares easy, but he's got friends with crossbows.

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Lovely. Tithe Road. We'll go by night, obviously, and knock at his window. He'll adore that.

choice.label: [Mime: frightened, not paid]
reply: Oh, I like you. Frightened it is. He took my money, after all. Only fair to take his sleep.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Back on the Books", on the Tithe Road. Jessamy is going, and Ash goes with her.

scenes.title: Noon
lines: It is noon. The plaza is full of honest people doing honest things. In the middle of it, Jessamy lies flat on her back on the cobbles, eyes shut, perfectly solid.
jessamy
Don't block it. Shift. You're in my sun.
jessamy
Fennick wrote me back in. Took him an hour, his hand was shakin' so bad. I stood over him and read every word.
jessamy
When he asked for my occupation, I told him to put "yes". So that's me, officially. Jessamy Leake, occupation: yes.
smug
jessamy
I'm sunburnt. It's horrible. I love it. Everything is so loud and yellow.
happy
jessamy
I'll still work nights, mind. Habit. But now it's 'cause I choose to.

choice.label: [Lie down on the cobbles next to her]
reply: There we are. Two layabouts in broad daylight. People are starin'. Let 'em. I've waited six years to be stared at.

choice.label: [Give her your hat]
reply: Oh, a gentleman. Or a lady. Whatever you are, you're a sweetheart. I'm not wearing it. I'm keeping it.

odile.likes_text: running a province (governor), or the books at the Command Table
odile.dislikes_text: dealing with the Concord, and idleness

3.name: Fair Assessment
3.desc: +1 Gilt a day for every province you hold.

5.name: Clean Books
5.desc: Buildings and Wardlamps cost 20% less Gilt.

scenes.title: Opening Balance
lines: odile
Sit down. This will not hurt. Much. I am opening an account for you.
She has a fresh page ruled in red. At the top, in a strict and beautiful hand: ASH (provisional).
odile
Assets: one coat, one blade, an unreasonable amount of nerve. Liabilities: the Concord, the Blank, and roughly everyone.
odile
The Concord cannot tax you, because you do not exist. Professionally, I find that offensive. Personally, I find it rather wonderful.
smug
odile
Is there anything you would like to declare?

choice.label: [Declare the nerve]
reply: Noted. "Nerve, considerable, undeclared until now." I shall value it later. It is going to ruin my totals.

choice.label: [Put a pebble on the desk]
reply: A pebble. Grey. Unremarkable. I shall enter it at one copper and you will never see it again. That is taxation.

choice.label: [Shake your head]
reply: Nothing to declare. Everyone says that. Everyone is lying. It is quite all right. I shall find it.

scenes.title: A Tenth Is a Tenth
lines: odile
Tax collectors do not hate people. We love sums. People simply get between us and the sums.
odile
I did the job well. Fairly. A tithe is a tenth, and a tenth is a tenth whether one is a duke or a donkey.
odile
My mother taught me that. Chief Assessor Marguerite Penhallow. She checked my homework in red ink, then checked it again in black.
odile
I thought the numbers were the point. I thought if the sums were fair, the world was.
sad
odile
Quill finds that very sweet. Quill rounds up. I should like that on the record.
angry

choice.label: [Tap the page: still fair]
reply: Yes. Still fair. Even if nothing else is, the arithmetic is. One holds on to what one can.

choice.label: [Mime rounding up]
reply: Do not dare. One of you in this town is quite enough.

scenes.title: Four Gilt
lines: odile
The village they sent me to collect was Lowmere, on the Saltreed edge. "Collect" does not mean collect from.
odile
It means the Concord weighs what a place is worth against what it costs to keep it in the Ledger. If it comes out short, the line is struck. The Blank does the rest.
odile
I did the sums three times. Lowmere came out four Gilt short. Four. I had four Gilt in my purse.
odile
I paid it. The office sent it back: "Collectors may not hold an interest." The order went through. It was countersigned by my mother.
angry
She smooths the page flat with the side of her hand. Over and over, though it is already flat.
odile
That is when I understood the numbers were never the point. They were the pretext. So I took the ledger and left.

choice.label: [Put four coins on the desk]
reply: ...Don't. Oh, don't, that's... I shall have to enter that. Under something. I haven't a column for it.

choice.label: [Sit with her]
reply: Thank you. I am not... It's the red ink. It gets in one's eyes.

choice.label: [Point at the stolen ledger: use it]
reply: Oh, I mean to. Every line in here is a place they meant to sell. I intend to make every one of them very, very expensive.

end: odile
Leave the provinces to me. Every one you hold will pay its fair share. To us, for a change.

scenes.title: Settling Accounts
lines: odile
A letter came. Red ink, then black. She always checks twice.
odile
My mother is at Old Mill Crossing. She wishes to discuss "the return of Concord property". That means the ledger. I think it also means me.
odile
She will offer me my post back. She will offer to pretend none of this happened. She is very good at making lines disappear.
odile
I need to go. Not to give her anything. To settle up. Properly. Once.

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Thank you. Old Mill Crossing. I'll bring a spare pen. She always forgets hers, to see if I'll offer.

choice.label: [Hold out a hand: leave the ledger here]
reply: Yes. Good. Safer. She cannot take what I have not brought. You would make a decent collector. That is not a compliment.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "Settle the Account", at Old Mill Crossing. Odile is going, and Ash goes with her.

scenes.title: Reconciled
lines: odile
She came alone. No guards, no clerks. Older than I remembered. She'd brought her own pen this time.
odile
We argued in numbers for three hours. Then I audited her, right there in the inn, on the back of the menu.
odile
Every account balanced. All but one line, twenty-six years old. Ninety Gilt, quietly moved, to keep one village off the lists.
odile
Penhallow Mere. Where I was born. Forty years of perfect books, and my mother's only crime was me.
sad
odile
She did not apologise. Penhallows do not. She said, "Keep the ledger. Use it better than I did." Then she paid for the menu.
Odile turns Ash's account page around. Under Liabilities, everything is struck through. Under Assets there is one new line: ODILE.

choice.label: [Initial the page]
reply: Countersigned. Good. Now it is binding. You are stuck with me. That is how accounts work.

choice.label: [Bow]
reply: Get up. People will think I have fined you.

velvette.likes_text: talking to factions (envoy), and an audience (the party)
velvette.dislikes_text: being ignored, and dirty work (the Inkworks)

3.name: Pillow Talk
3.desc: Every standing gain with a faction is 1 bigger.

5.name: Encore
5.desc: The party's gauge fills 15% faster on missions.

scenes.title: A Secret for a Secret
lines: velvette
Darling. Close the door. No, leave it open a crack. People should know we are in here together. It is good for my reputation.
smug
Her dressing table is a battlefield of powder and rouge, with a rapier laid across it like a hairbrush.
velvette
House rules of the Crimson Encore: I tell you a secret, you tell me one. Business, I have done it that way since I was sixteen.
velvette
Mine: Bran sleeps with his contract arm under the pillow. He talks to it. Tenderly.
velvette
Your turn. ...Oh. You have nothing to tell. No past at all. Tragic, mon petit. Or thrilling. I have not decided.
surprised

choice.label: [Lean in as if to whisper, then say nothing]
reply: Oh, you tease. You absolute professional. Silence is the most expensive secret there is. I put it on your tab.

choice.label: [Draw a small X in the powder on her mirror]
reply: An X. A kiss, or a mark on a map? Don't tell me. I'll enjoy guessing.

choice.label: [Look at the rapier]
reply: Don't touch the sword, darling. It is the only one in the room who isn't flirting with you.

scenes.title: The Closing Act
lines: velvette
Every night at the Encore ended with the closing act. A real duel, live blades, against a volunteer from the house.
velvette
Rich men, mostly. Bored ones. They paid a fortune to cross swords with the star. Most went home with a scratch and a story.
velvette
Some went home lighter. Enfin, you would be amazed what a man confesses with a rapier at his throat and four hundred people watching.
smug
velvette
I wrote it all down. Who owed whom, who loved whom, who was skimming the Concord's tithe. Then I sold it back to them, one page at a time.
velvette
Don't look at me like that. A secret, it is only dangerous while one person owns it. I am a public service.

choice.label: [Applaud slowly]
reply: Merci, merci. You may throw roses. Not literally, the thorns ruin the silk.

choice.label: [Hold out a hand: show me the book]
reply: Ha! No. Nobody touches the book. Not even Ottoline. Especially not Ottoline, she would use it to prop a door.

scenes.title: Eleven Volunteers
lines: No powder tonight. Without it she looks younger, and very tired.
velvette
Here is a secret I never sold, because nobody could afford it.
velvette

Some of the volunteers weren't volunteers. The Concord's Office of Quiet paid the Encore to seat certain names in the front row. A judge. A printer. A poet who'd rhymed "Concord" with something unkind.
velvette
I was told it was theatre. A little blood, a big bow. Then the first one didn't get up, and the house rose and cheered, and my impresario wept for joy at the takings.
sad
velvette
Eleven. Knew by the third. Kept going. Other choice was being the twelfth.
velvette
When the Blank took Lantern Row I was almost glad. That's ugly. Never said it out loud before.

choice.label: [Stay. Don't look away]
reply: ...You didn't flinch. Everyone flinches, darling. Even me, in the mirror. Thank you.

choice.label: [Put a hand on her shoulder]
reply: Careful. People who comfort me end up in my book. ...No. Not you. I leave you out.

choice.label: [Step back]
reply: Yes. The sensible reaction. Sensible people, I have always found them terribly dull. Bonne nuit.

end: velvette
Send me to your factions. I know where all their bodies are buried. In a few cases, because I buried them.
smug

scenes.title: The Impresario
lines: velvette
Augustin Sallow. My impresario. The man who chose the volunteers and counted the takings.
velvette
He didn't go down with Lantern Row. Of course not. He runs a showboat in the Saltreed Marsh now, the Gilded Heron. New star. Same closing act.
velvette
He keeps the Office of Quiet's commissions in his cabin. Every name, every price, and my stage name at the bottom of each: "the instrument".
angry
velvette
I would like to give one last performance. One he did not book.

choice.label: [Nod]
reply: Lovely. Saltreed Marsh. I need you, a costume and a very quiet boat.

choice.label: [Mime: don't kill him]
reply: ...You ask a lot. Fine. I leave him breathing. I leave him a great many other things too, mostly bruises.

end: A personal mission is on the Command Table: "The Last Performance", in Saltreed Marsh. Fauvette is going, and Ash goes with her.

scenes.title: Curtain Call
lines: velvette
The Gilded Heron had a full house. I came on during the closing act. In costume, naturellement. One has standards.
velvette
I challenged Augustin with the whole Marsh watching. He'd never held a sword in his life. I let him keep his. Then I read the commissions aloud. Every name. Every price.
velvette
Eleven names, read slow. And the audience didn't cheer. They took their hats off. Best show I ever gave.
sad
velvette
Augustin is on his way to the Concord with the book pinned to his coat. Voilà. Let us see how they reward a man who keeps receipts.
smug
velvette
One more thing. House rules: a secret for a secret. I owe you one since the first night.
She leans in and says it in Ash's ear: her real name. It is a very ordinary name. Nobody else will ever hear it.

choice.label: [Keep it]
reply: Good. Only secret I ever gave away. Don't you dare sell it. ...Well. Not for less than it's worth.

choice.label: [Kiss her hand]
reply: Oh, now you flirt. Enfin. I was starting to think you were just very polite furniture.
